takeaways.label: Record dispatches, margin expansion
takeaways.text: ~1,900 machines shipped in Q2, the highest ever, while standalone EBITDA margin rose 320 bps YoY to 28% despite a higher share of entry-level machines.

takeaways.label: PLI scheme unlocks vertical integration
takeaways.text: Approval for a ₹1,020 crore investment with 25% capital incentive positions Jyoti to develop in-house CNC controllers, motors and drives, a step toward becoming a mechatronics company.

takeaways.label: Huron ramp-up is the H2 catalyst
takeaways.text: Dispatches from expanded Huron capacity begin in Q3, with ₹80–100 crores expected that quarter and a path to the ~₹300 crore full-year target, though end-user certificate progress remains a watchpoint.

takeaways.label: Order book and demand visibility support multi-year growth
takeaways.text: A ₹5,082 crore order book plus management's stated 3-year demand confidence, anchored in auto/EV capex and import substitution, underpin the 25–30% CAGR ambition.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether Huron dispatches actually hit the ₹80–100 crore Q3 run-rate, whether the foundry commences operations on time, and whether the aerospace & defence tenders that slipped in Q2 reopen and convert.

points.label: Q2 revenue and unrecognized backlog
points.text: Huron contributed ~₹44 crores of revenue in Q2, while ~₹65 crores of prior dispatches remain unrecognized in consolidation due to POCM accounting and pending end-user certificates.

points.label: Capacity expansion now live
points.text: New manufacturing capacity added in November 2025; dispatches from this expanded base are expected to commence in Q3 and Q4 FY27.

points.label: End-user certificate progress
points.text: 1–2 machines received government permissions for dispatch last week; management stated there has been no further communication from European investigative authorities since its response to the April notice.

points.label: Q3 and full-year trajectory
points.text: Q3 dispatches are projected at ₹80–100 crores, with further ramp-up in Q4, keeping the company on track to reach close to ₹300 crores for the full year once clearance and certificate clarity arrive.

quotes.text: Parakramsinh Jadeja: "So the first week of April, what we received the notice and what we have response to them, and then after there is not a single communication from them, okay. And this is the same status are all other investigative company in Europe."

points.label: PLI approval secured
points.text: Jyoti received approval under the government's PLI scheme for domestic manufacturing, committing over ₹1,020 crores of capital investment over 5 years with a 25% capital incentive (₹255 crores) to develop in-house manufacturing of CNC controllers, motors, drives, and operator interfaces.

points.label: ECMS subsidy adds further support
points.text: The company also received a capital subsidy under the ECMS scheme for electronics component manufacturing, with phase 1 entailing a ₹400–450 crore investment and a ₹200 crore net outlay after subsidy.

points.label: State subsidy expected soon
points.text: A Gujarat government matching grant plus an R&D subsidy are anticipated, which would take the total subsidy to over 50% of the ₹1,020 crore PLI investment.

points.label: Controller R&D already underway
points.text: A dedicated controller division within the R&D center has been working for 1.5 years with a team of 110+ engineers; 40–50 more are expected to be added in the next ~6 months, with own controllers targeted within 2 years.

points.label: Strategic ambition
points.text: Management aims to transform Jyoti from a mechanical company into a mechatronics company within 2 years, developing all electronics in-house, and subsequently enter industrial automation with robotics as the first priority.

points.label: Customer acceptance risk acknowledged
points.text: Management noted the challenge of customer acceptance for own controllers but pointed to a base of 15,000+ customers, with roughly one-third described as "die-hard" customers willing to test new offerings.

quotes.text: Parakramsinh Jadeja: "Today, we are a mechanical company. We design the machine, we manufacture the machine, we castings, we machining the precision component, and we integrate. Now in future, we are looking to be a mechatronics company."

points.label: Standalone margin strength
points.text: Standalone EBITDA margin reached 28% in Q2 FY27, up 320 bps YoY, driven by the business model's ability to sustain margins not below 25% even as the share of entry-level machines increases.

points.label: Consolidated margin and H2 path
points.text: Consolidated EBITDA margin stood at 21.8% in Q2; management expressed confidence in reaching the guided 25% for the full year, citing H2's seasonal strength and the Huron ramp-up contribution.

points.label: Operational leverage ahead
points.text: Close to 950 people were added in the last 6 months, with costs being booked now while associated revenue is still to come, implying margin tailwinds as those people become productive.

points.label: R&D investment from margin gains
points.text: Margin improvements from vertical integration and operational leverage will be reinvested into R&D; cost advantages are expected from in-house manufacturing of vertically integrated components.

points.label: Interest cost declining
points.text: Interest cost fell to ~₹14 crores in Q2 due to improved working capital utilization; management confirmed interest is fully expensed and expected to remain stable quarter-to-quarter.

quotes.text: Parakramsinh Jadeja: "I was always telling to you people in your past questions and in a meeting, that let's say once this our entry-level product number is also going to increase, our business model combination is such that we will not go below 25% of margin there."

points.label: Record order intake
points.text: Q2 order intake reached ₹800 crores, driven by strong demand from the auto sector where OEMs are adding capacity, particularly in the EV space.

points.label: Order book visibility
points.text: A total order book of ₹5,082 crores provides strong revenue visibility for the coming quarters.

points.label: Multi-year demand confidence
points.text: Management stated it is "very much confident" of demand visibility for the next 3 years, with the front-end business side facing no challenge; the focus is entirely on improving execution.

points.label: Import substitution tailwind
points.text: With ~60% of India's CNC machine demand still met through imports, management sees a significant opportunity for domestic manufacturers to capture share.

points.label: Aerospace & defence pipeline intact
points.text: Order intake from aerospace & defence declined in Q2 because some government tenders were not opened as expected; management stated no orders were lost and further orders are expected in Q3 and coming quarters.

points.label: EMS execution improving
points.text: Execution of EMS orders improved in Q2, with further improvement expected in the next two quarters as new capacity comes online.

quotes.text: Parakramsinh Jadeja: "I think, momentum, what the way we are seeing the investments are coming and pipelines are what we are seeing today. We are very much confident in the next 3 years, we are clearly visibilities are there."

points.label: Foundry nearing completion
points.text: The new foundry, using lost foam vacuum casting technology capable of up to 15-tonne single-piece casting, is on the last mile; equipment is under transit and expected to reach month-end, with completion expected this quarter.

points.label: Foundry capacity expansion
points.text: Monthly capacity will expand from 1,500 tonnes to 5,000 tonnes once the new foundry is operational.

points.label: New plant status
points.text: Machine assembly and sheet metal facilities have already been put to use; management stated there is no bottleneck for current-year targets.

points.label: Inventory days improving
points.text: Inventory days improved from 203 days at March levels to close to 190 days currently, with further reduction expected by year-end.

points.label: Cash flow strengthening
points.text: Operating cash flow reached 47% of EBITDA in H1, up from a very low base last year, attributed to better working capital management; management is targeting 50% OCF/EBITDA by year-end and maintained going forward.

points.label: New product launch
points.text: The MTX 100, a compact 5-axis multitasking turn-mill center combining turning, milling, gear cutting and grinding in a single setup, was launched for aerospace, defence, automotive & EV, and oil & gas industries.

points.label: FY27 volume target
points.text: 8,000 machines for the full year, with H2 implied at ~4,700+ machines; management pushed back on the characterization of this as "conservative," noting that H2 volume alone nearly equals last year's full-year figure of 5,600.

points.label: FY27 revenue growth
points.text: 25% to 30% combined growth (Huron plus Jyoti) remains on track.

points.label: Medium-term growth ambition
points.text: 25% to 30% CAGR targeted for the next 2–3 years.

points.label: Average realization stability
points.text: Average realization is expected to maintain the ₹35–36 lakh range over the next 2–3 years, though the current quarter saw a reduction to about ₹32 lakhs.

points.label: Supply chain resilience
points.text: Management credited proper planning and maintained safety-factor inventories for the ability to clock current growth despite broader supply chain challenges; own controllers are not part of the near-term supply plan.

items.title: Group growth guide
items.text: Management targets 25-30% revenue growth over the next two to three years on the back of the completed expansion, with EBITDA margin not falling below 25% even at full utilisation. On FY26 revenue of ₹2,286 crore, that implies roughly ₹2,900-3,000 crore in FY27, supported by an order book of ₹5,082 crore at September 2026.

items.title: Rajkot 10,000-machine ramp
items.text: The ₹400-450 crore addition of 10,000 machines per annum at Rajkot started commercial operation in Q2 FY27, lifting capacity from 6,000 to 16,000 machines and already enabling record quarterly dispatches of ~1,900 machines. Management reaffirmed a FY27 target of ~8,000 machines (H1: 3,317 vs 5,600 in all of FY26), with order booking pace set to rise now that capacity is in place.

items.title: Huron France ramp-up
items.text: The expanded Strasbourg facility, Huron's first capacity addition since 2007, commenced operations in November 2025 with first dispatches from new assembly expected from Q3-Q4 FY27. Management guides Huron to ₹300-325 crore revenue at 6-10% EBITDA margin in FY27, with ₹80-100 crore of dispatches in Q3 alone.

items.title: Huron export-license revenue release
items.text: ₹65 crore of reversed Huron revenue (from a ₹67 crore Q4 FY26 prudence reversal) remains pending recognition, with end-user certificates progressing and one or two machines receiving permissions just before the Q2 FY27 call. Once licenses clear, the revenue and ~₹40 crore of margin flow into H2, adding 3-4% to consolidated EBITDA margin.

items.title: ECMS electronics backward integration
items.text: Jyoti received Meity approval (17 August 2026) for ₹1,020.65 crore of investment over five years to build in-house CNC controllers, motors and drives, with a 25% central subsidy (~₹255 crore) and an expected matching Gujarat grant taking total support to 50%+. The first ₹400-450 crore phase carries a net outlay of only ~₹200 crore, and in-house controllers should cut import costs and lift margins from FY29.

items.title: Foundry startup
items.text: The new lost-form vacuum casting foundry at Rajkot was to commence "in the coming days" as of the November 2026 call, taking total foundry capacity from ~1,500 to 5,000 tonnes per month - the first in India able to cast 15-ton single pieces. In-house castings remove a supply bottleneck for the 16,000-machine capacity and support the ₹450-500 crore FY27 capex plan's last mile.

items.title: EMS vertical scale-up
items.text: EMS is 12% of the ₹5,082 crore order book with execution improving in Q2 FY27 as new capacity comes on stream, and management targets 20-25% of the portfolio from EMS in coming years against a sector expected to need over one lakh CNC machines in five years. Dollar-linked pricing on the EMS order book should yield better margins on execution.
